officialRequirement: Describe the physiological reactions electrical shock causes
lesson: The four quantities and the circuit they describe
teachingSection: W01-CETA-v16.3 · Shock physiology, emergency response, and First Aid boundaries
teachingLevel: v16.3 integrated lesson: subject-specific technical instruction, instructional visual, worked examples, guided practice, changed independent scenario, knowledge checks, and required semantic evidence.
guidedPractice: A 3.3 V source is applied to 1.5 kOhm. Calculate current, then state whether 1 mA or 10 mA is the more sensible mental estimate before calculating. | A resistor carries 20 mA with 5 V across it. Find resistance and power. masteryEvidence: Correct auto-graded lesson checks where applicable; topic-specific constructed-response/performance evidence; changed-context practice; weekly cumulative mastery; physical evidence when required.
laboratoryEvidence: LAB-001: Calculation with units, pre-power checklist, circuit/simulation image, measured voltage and current, percent difference, and one troubleshooting observation. Physical proficiency is credited only on the physical route.

requiredSubjectKnowledge: Recognize shock effects can include involuntary contraction, burns, respiratory or cardiac effects; Do not touch a person who may still be energized; Call emergency services and remove energy only by a safe trained method; Use CPR/AED/First Aid only within training and authorization; State that electrical injury may require medical evaluation even when external burns look limited
